subject: chemistry
title: Redox in terms of electrons
key_idea: (Higher tier) Oxidation is the loss of electrons and reduction is the gain of electrons. Displacement reactions are redox reactions, and ionic equations show only the particles that change.

sections.heading: Oxidation and reduction as electron transfer

blocks.text: (Higher tier) This section covers oxidation and reduction in terms of electrons and half equations.

items.meaning: An equation showing one particle losing or gaining electrons.

items: A metal atom is oxidised when it loses electrons to form a positive ion.
A positive ion is reduced when it gains electrons to form an atom.
A non-metal atom is reduced when it gains electrons to form a negative ion.
Oxidation and reduction always happen together, so the reaction is a **redox reaction**.

blocks.label: Half equations
blocks.formula:
Na → Na⁺ + e⁻
Fe³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Fe
Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻
2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2e⁻
where: Na → Na⁺ + e⁻: sodium is oxidised
Fe³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Fe: iron(III) ions are reduced

blocks.text: Electrons are on the right in oxidation and on the left in reduction.

diagram.alt: Sort each half equation into oxidation or reduction.
diagram.prompt: Is each half equation oxidation or reduction?

items: Oxidation is loss of electrons. Reduction is gain of electrons.
Name the particle: an atom or an ion, not the whole compound.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) In a displacement reaction a more reactive metal transfers electrons to the ions of a less reactive metal.

items.meaning: An equation that shows only the particles that change in a reaction.
An ion that is present but does not change, so it is left out of the ionic equation.

items.lead: Split the aqueous compounds into ions.
items.text: Zn + Cu²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → Zn²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ + Cu
Sulfate ions, SO₄²⁻, are on both sides and do not change.

items: Zinc atoms lose two electrons: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻. Zinc is **oxidised**.
Copper ions gain two electrons: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. Copper ions are **reduced**.
The same pattern applies to magnesium displacing zinc: Mg(s) + Zn²⁺(aq) → Mg²⁺(aq) + Zn(s).
A displacement reaction is a redox reaction because one particle loses electrons and another gains them.
In a displacement reaction the more reactive metal is oxidised and the ions of the less reactive metal are reduced.
Leave spectator ions out of an ionic equation.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) The same ideas apply to metals reacting with acids and to halogen displacement.

items: Acids react with some metals, such as magnesium, zinc and iron, to produce a salt and hydrogen.
In Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂ the magnesium atoms lose two electrons, so they are oxidised.
The hydrogen ions gain electrons, so they are reduced: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂.
In Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + Br₂ chlorine gains electrons and is reduced. Bromide ions lose electrons and are oxidised.
(Edexcel) A reaction in which no particle gains or loses electrons is not redox. Copper in CuO and in CuSO₄ is Cu²⁺ both times, so it is neither oxidised nor reduced.
Check whether any particle gains or loses electrons. If so, it is a redox reaction.
Hydrogen ions are reduced when a metal reacts with an acid.

checks.q: Magnesium displaces zinc from zinc sulfate solution. Write the ionic equation with state symbols.
In the equation in the previous question, which particles are oxidised and which are reduced? Give a reason for each.
checks.a: Magnesium atoms are oxidised because they lose electrons. Zinc ions are reduced because they gain electrons.

checks.q: Write a half equation to show that sodium is oxidised.

exam_phrases: magnesium (atoms) are oxidised because they lose electrons
zinc (ions) are reduced because they gain electrons

mistakes.wrong: The reaction at the negative electrode is electrolysis.
mistakes.right: Electrolysis is ignored. Say reduction, because hydrogen ions gain electrons.

mistakes.wrong: Magnesium atoms lose electrons and zinc ions gain electrons.
mistakes.right: This scores only 1 mark. Also say the magnesium atoms are oxidised and the zinc ions are reduced.

mistakes.wrong: Mg(s) + Zn²⁺(aq) → Mg²⁺(aq) + Zn(s) written without state symbols.
mistakes.right: The question asks for state symbols. With them missing or incorrect, only 1 mark is allowed for the correct species.

worked_example.question:
Magnesium reacts with iron chloride solution.

3 Mg + 2 FeCl₃ → 2 Fe + 3 MgCl₂

Explain which species is reduced in the reaction between magnesium and iron chloride.

Your answer should include the half equation for the reduction.
answer_points: Because reduction is gain of electrons (or a change in oxidation state from +3 to 0).
worked_example.tip: One mark each. Name the ion, state the definition, then write the half equation.

exam_phrases: redox involves both reduction and oxidation
zinc (atoms) lose electrons and are oxidised
copper (ions) gain electrons and are reduced
chlorine gains electrons to form a chloride ion
the copper (ions) do not lose or gain electrons

mistakes.wrong: Copper sulfate is reduced because it gains electrons.
mistakes.right: Copper sulfate is reduced is ignored. Name the particle: copper ions gain electrons and are reduced.
Cadmium atoms gaining electrons is rejected. Cadmium ions, Cd²⁺, gain electrons. Zinc atoms lose electrons.

mistakes.wrong: The reaction is redox because zinc gains oxygen.
mistakes.right: References to loss and gain of oxygen are ignored. Explain in terms of electrons.

worked_example.question:
Small amounts of some metals are extracted using displacement reactions.

In one process, zinc dust is used to precipitate cadmium metal from a solution containing cadmium ions.

Cd²⁺(aq) + Zn(s) → Cd(s) + Zn²⁺(aq)

Explain why this displacement reaction can be described as a redox reaction.
answer_points: Zinc (atoms) lose electrons and are oxidised.
Cadmium ions (Cd²⁺) gain electrons and are reduced.
worked_example.tip: The first mark is given even if the species are wrong. Do not say zinc ions or cadmium atoms.

exam_phrases: atoms are oxidised to form positive ions
atoms lose electrons to form positive ions
atoms are reduced to form negative ions
atoms gain electrons to form negative ions

mistakes.wrong: Atoms are reduced to form positive ions.
mistakes.right: Atoms are oxidised to form positive ions, by losing electrons. Atoms are reduced to form negative ions, by gaining electrons.
The balancing mark needs the electrons: 2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2e⁻.

worked_example.question:
Atoms are either oxidised or reduced to form ions.

Complete the sentences about how atoms form ions. Choose from: oxidised, reduced, lose, gain.

Atoms are ______ to form positive ions. Atoms ______ electrons to form positive ions.

Atoms are ______ to form negative ions. Atoms ______ electrons to form negative ions.
answer_points: Atoms are oxidised to form positive ions. Atoms lose electrons to form positive ions.
Atoms are reduced to form negative ions. Atoms gain electrons to form negative ions.
worked_example.tip: Oxidised and reduced together score 1 mark. Lose and gain together score 1 mark. They are marked independently.
